overview: This Senate resolution names August 22 through August 30, 2026, National Park Week. The week includes August 25, the anniversary of the 1916 law that created the National Park Service, the federal agency that manages national parks, battlefields and historic sites in every state. The resolution notes that national parks drew more than 323 million recreational visits in 2025 and are important to local economies, and it praises Park Service employees for protecting these places. It encourages people in the United States and around the world to visit and support the parks responsibly. It does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it on August 6, 2026.
for: Supporters say the week celebrates places that belong to all Americans and encourages people to visit and help protect them for future generations.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and does nothing directly about the parks' staffing or maintenance needs.
